newsitem.title: INDIA: Delhi shares end lower on budget fears.
newsitem.headline: Delhi shares end lower on budget fears.

text.p: Delhi shares closed lower on Tuesday on selling by foreign institutional investors (FIIs) and speculators triggered by uncertainty over the federal budget, brokers said.
The Delhi Stock Exchange sensitive index dipped 1.72 points to close at 798.62.
"The market is likely to remain sluggish in the short term and should recover after the passage of the financial budget in parliament," said Harish Malhotra of brokers Malhotra Financial Services.
Last week, Prime Minister Inder Kumar Gujral's cabinet adopted the 1997/98 budget which former finance minister P. Chidambaram presented to parliament on February 28.

But four leftwing parties in the alliance Front said on Monday that they wanted changes in the areas of insurance, taxes, divestment in state enterprises, public distribution, customs duties and excise duties.
The budget was widely applauded by economists and sparked a stock market rally after it was unveiled in February by the previous administration of H.D. Deve Gowda.
Reliance Industries ended a shade higher at 304.55 rupees on selective buying and selling by speculators, brokers said.
State Bank of India fell 1.65 rupees to 314.60.
ACC drifted 8.75 rupees lower to 1,468.00 rupees.
